data.title: KLN Honoured by Frost & Sullivan as 2026 Asia-Pacific Logistics Company of the Year for 10th Consecutive Year
data.description:
HONG KONG, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- KLN Logistics Group Limited ('KLN'; Stock Code 0636.HK) has been awarded the 2026 Asia-Pacific Logistics Company of the Year for the tenth consecutive year at the 2026 Frost & Sullivan Best Practices Recognition (the 'Recognition'). The award presentation ceremony was held in Singapore on 18 November 2026.

The Recognition, presented by global business consulting firm Frost & Sullivan, honours innovative companies that demonstrate market-leading performance and unrivalled customer service. It acknowledges KLN's market leadership, operational excellence, customer-centric approach and capability to deliver integrated supply chain solutions across the region. It also highlights KLN's resilient performance in driving growth and innovation in an evolving logistics landscape.

Vic Cheung, Executive Director and CEO of KLN, said, "We are delighted to receive the award for the tenth consecutive year. This sustained recognition is a testament to our teams' dedication and our unwavering focus on delivering agile, innovative, and customer-centric logistics solutions. As we continue to embrace new technologies, we remain committed to driving transformational growth, and creating long-term value for our customers and stakeholders across the Asia Pacific region and beyond."

Wong Siew Loong, Executive Director and COO of KLN, also served as a panellist in Frost & Sullivan's leadership roundtable. The panel, themed "AI as a Catalyst for Transformational Growth", explored how artificial intelligence is reshaping business models, operational efficiency and competitive advantage in the logistics industry.

About KLN Logistics Group Limited (Stock Code 0636.HK)

KLN is an Asia-rooted, global 3PL delivering customer-centric, end-to-end supply chain solutions that connect markets and power global trade, as a trusted partner to many of the top 100 global brands and Fortune Global 500 companies across a wide spectrum of industries. With a presence across 59 countries and territories, KLN offers integrated logistics, international freight forwarding, e-commerce and industrial project logistics solutions. KLN has been the global No. 1 Trans-Pacific NVOCC from Asia to the US since 2023 and ranks No. 20 among Global 3PLs (Armstrong & Associates, 2026). Listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, KLN generated revenue* of over HK$56 billion in 2025 and is a constituent of the Hang Seng Corporate Sustainability Benchmark Index. Learn more at www.kln.com

*For continuing operations only

SOURCE KLN Logistics Group Limited

data.title: KKR Invests in India Renewables Business Run by Petronas-Backed Gentari
data.description:
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Investment firm KKR has made a minority investment in a renewable-energy platform in India run by Gentari, an entity established by Malaysia's national oil and gas company.

The investment will provide growth capital to support the renewables platform's continued expansion in India, KKR and Gentari said Thursday.

No terms were disclosed.

KKR has been investing in India's infrastructure sector for more than a decade, and has committed more than $27 billion to energy-transition and renewables infrastructure globally since 2011.

The deal with Gentari--part of Petronas Group--aims to capture the need for continued investment in India's energy infrastructure as demand for reliable power grows rapidly.

"We believe scaled platforms that can deliver increasingly sophisticated renewable energy solutions will have an important role to play in meeting that demand," said Hardik Shah, Asia-Pacific infrastructure partner at KKR.

Gentari's India platform has about 8 gigawatts of operating, under-construction and contracted renewable-energy capacity. Its portfolio spans solar, wind, hybrid and battery-energy storage solutions.

Gentari Group Chief Executive Sushil Purohit said that with KKR's support, it is well-positioned to keep scaling the business.

Following the investment, Gentari will retain strategic oversight and operational control of the platform, the companies said.

The tie-up comes on the heels of KKR's roughly $16 billion partnership with RWE investing in offshore-wind farms in the U.K.

data.title: Citigroup CEO Fraser warns of more tech outages as firms patch tech
data.description:
• Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser cautioned that tech outages risk becoming more routine as companies race to patch their systems and tighten security.
  • “The volume of changes — the patches — that is going through the world’s tech stack at the same time is five- to 10-fold what we’ve ever seen before,” Fraser said at a Bloomberg Newsmakers event Wednesday.
  • “We should be expecting for a while some more downtime, some more outages in different areas.” Fraser said she is not surprised by recent tech outages across the US. 
  • Large U.S. bank stock prices neared the rare 'death cross' bearish technical chart pattern recently, with the KBW Bank Index's 50-day moving average almost falling below its 200-day moving average. The index was down as much as 2.4% on Nov. 17, a day after JPMorgan Chase faced a "technical issue" that had caused customers' transactions to take longer to process on Monday. Other bank stocks, such as Bank of America , US Bank , and Wells Fargo , were also impacted.

data.title: Microsoft, Intel Expand Azure Infrastructure Partnership Under Long-Term Agreement
data.description:
REDMOND (dpa-AFX) - Microsoft Corporation (MSFT) said it has expanded its long-term partnership with Intel to strengthen Azure infrastructure and support growing demand for cloud and AI computing.

Under the agreement, Microsoft will secure multi-year supplies of Intel Xeon processors, including next-generation server CPUs codenamed Diamond Rapids. The companies will also expand their work on Azure infrastructure and Intel-based hardware systems.

Microsoft said it will become the first company to use Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for its custom Azure chips.

The collaboration will also cover Intel Xeon processors with Compute Express Link (CXL), Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) and confidential computing, aimed at improving memory efficiency, database performance and security.

'Our longstanding collaboration with Intel brings together advanced packaging, custom compute, memory and security capabilities to support Azure and drive continued innovation. Together, we are combining silicon and systems engineering to meet growing customer demand for cloud and AI computing,' said Saurabh Dighe, CVP, Azure System & Architecture at Microsoft.

On the Nasdaq, Microsoft shares rose 0.70% in after-hours trading after closing at $508.29 on Wednesday.

data.title: Australia shares drop as miner rout deepens, jobs data fuels slowdown worries
data.description:
Key points:
  • ASX 200 records lowest close since October 15
  • Miners hit near 8-month low
  • Banks end 0.3% lower, paring some earlier losses
  • Soft jobs print lowers rate hike risk, fuels downturn worries

By Shruti Agarwal

Australian shares logged their lowest closing level in over a month on Thursday, as the rout in miners deepened, while weak jobs data that largely removed the risk of rate hikes fed concerns about an economic downturn.

The S&P/ASX 200 index ended 1% lower at 8,730.40 points, its lowest closing level since October 15. The benchmark is down 3.9% so far this week. All but two sectors ended in the red.

Miners hit a near eight-month low, dropping 4%, with heavyweights BHP and Rio Tinto shedding 4.1% and 3.7%, respectively.

In the previous session, copper had its biggest one-day drop since the April 2025 US tariff selloff due to inflation fears, though it has since recovered slightly.

The gold producers' sub-index fell 5.6% to a more than three-month low.

The materials sector has lost roughly 7% this week as rotation out of the sector intensified.

Data showed employment in the country fell for a second straight month in October, while the jobless rate rose to a fresh five-year high, easing concerns about a tight labour market.

The soft print nearly wiped out bets on further rate hikes, and markets are now pricing in a 2.4% chance of a cut at the central bank's December meeting, up from none before the data.

While the data removes rate risk, it also signals slower household spending and weaker earnings growth into 2027, said William Taylor, chief operating officer at ETF Shares.

"That's why we're not seeing the relief rally you might expect," he said.

RBA board members, who voted against a hike this month, had flagged the risk of the economy facing a sharper-than-expected downturn, worries reinforced by mounting evidence of broader layoffs and persistently weak productivity growth.

Financials pared some losses after the data but still ended 0.3% lower.

The rate outlook eases concerns about mortgage stress and bad debts, but a continued rise in unemployment could shift the focus to credit quality, a tougher backdrop for the sector, Taylor said.

New Zealand's benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index slipped 0.1% to 14,247.25 points.

data.title: South African rand slides to year low ahead of rate decision
data.description:
The South African rand weakened to its lowest level of the year against the dollar on Thursday, pressured by a firmer greenback, softer precious-metal prices and uncertainty around local government coalition talks, as investors awaited the central bank's policy decision later in the day.

  • At 0402 GMT, the rand traded at 17.3450 against the dollar , 0.3% weaker than its previous close and near the year's low of 17.36 touched in Asian trade

  • The risk-sensitive rand has come under pressure in recent months amid broader risk aversion, while coalition talks following local government elections have raised questions about the stability of South Africa's Government of National Unity as the African National Congress and Democratic Alliance work to finalise local power-sharing agreements

  • "The local elections are also causing a massive headache, as has the move in commodities," said Adam Phillips of Umkhulu Treasury

  • The dollar hovered near a 19-month high after minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting and hawkish comments from a Fed official reinforced expectations of further interest-rate hikes, weighing on precious metals and leaving South Africa's key export, gold, near a 14-month low

  • Focus later in the session will turn to the South African Reserve Bank's interest-rate decision due around 1300 GMT, where it is widely expected to leave rates unchanged after raising them at its previous meeting

  • South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) was steady in early deals, with the yield at 8.71%
